subject.title: feat(agents): rename scheduler agent tool cron -> automations

question: Should the public scheduler-tool identifier retain a temporary `cron` invocation alias, or should OpenClaw ship this as an explicitly versioned breaking MCP/tool-schema change?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes a callable tool identifier while preserving only stored policy data; source inspection cannot determine whether existing MCP callers and in-flight tool use are an accepted breaking-change population.

options.title: Stage the rename with an invocation alias
options.body: Advertise `automations` while accepting `cron` at the dispatcher/MCP boundary for a documented deprecation window, with focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Approve a versioned breaking rename
options.body: Keep the no-alias behavior only with explicit maintainer approval, protocol/versioning treatment, and upgrade documentation for existing callers.

recommendation.title: Stage the rename with an invocation alias
recommendation.body: Advertise `automations` while accepting `cron` at the dispatcher/MCP boundary for a documented deprecation window, with focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC-linked migration design and can provide the implementation context; a repository maintainer must make the final product-contract choice.
